description: One quart holds 4 cups. Convert quarts to cups and back, with the table for half quarts up to two gallons, and worked examples for soup and stock.

faqs.answer: 4 cups. A quart is a quarter of a gallon, and a gallon holds 16 cups, so a quarter is 4.
faqs.question: How many cups are in a quart?

faqs.answer: 2 cups. Half a quart is a pint, and a pint is 2 cups.
faqs.question: How many cups are in half a quart?

faqs.answer: No, but close. A US quart is 946 ml, and a liter is 1000 ml, so a liter is about 6 percent more than a quart.
faqs.question: Is a quart the same as a liter?

faqs.answer: 32 fluid ounces. A quart is 4 cups, and each cup is 8 fluid ounces, so 4 times 8 is 32.
faqs.question: How many fluid ounces are in a quart?

faqs.answer: 4 quarts. A gallon is 16 cups, and each quart is 4 cups, so 16 divided by 4 is 4.
faqs.question: How many quarts are in a gallon?

felicityNote: The quart carton is the measure. When a soup recipe says 3 quarts of stock, I buy three cartons and pour them in, no jug needed.

howToSteps.name: Read the quarts
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in quarts in your recipe or on the carton. Halves and whole numbers are the usual amounts.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 4
howToSteps.text: Quarts times 4 gives cups. One quart is 4 cups, two quarts is 8 cups, three quarts is 12 cups.

howToSteps.name: Count the cartons
howToSteps.text: A quart carton is 4 cups. Two quart cartons is 8 cups. For stock and milk, the carton is the measure.

howToSteps.name: Check liters separately
howToSteps.text: A quart is 946 ml, not a liter. If the recipe is metric, 1 liter is 1.06 quarts, just over 4 cups.

name: Quarts to Cups
title: Quarts to Cups: Volume Converter
tutorial: One quart is 4 cups. The name gives it away: a quart is a quarter of a gallon, and a gallon holds 16 cups, so a quarter of 16 is 4. A quart is also 2 pints and 32 fluid ounces, which makes it the middle step in the whole US volume ladder.

Quarts are the unit on the containers in the fridge. Milk, stock, broth, and cream come in quart cartons, and yogurt comes in quart tubs. A recipe that calls for a quart of stock is asking for 4 cups, which is exactly one quart carton, poured straight in.

Soup and stock are where the conversion earns its keep. A pot of soup that serves eight needs about 3 quarts of liquid, which is 12 cups. A recipe doubled from 2 cups of broth to 4 cups has used exactly one quart. Thinking in quarts keeps the big numbers small.

A quart is close to a liter but not equal to one. A US quart is 946 ml, so a liter is about 6 percent more than a quart. A recipe that says 1 liter of stock needs 1.06 quarts, which is just over 4 cups.

The quart is also the size of the air fryer basket question. A 4-quart basket holds 16 cups, a 6-quart basket holds 24 cups. The basket sizes on the box are quarts, and the food going in is measured in cups, so the conversion runs both ways in the same kitchen.
